create-entry.name: Create-entry action
create-entry.acceptance: An entry step `{"op": "create", "entry_type": …, "title": …, "data": {…}, "status": "draft"}` creates a schema-validated entry, returns `entry_id`/`slug` as step output, emits entry_created at depth+1, previews in a dry run, and never duplicates on a retried run (idempotency key = run + step).

custom-operation.name: Free-form AI operation
custom-operation.acceptance: An operation step can carry its own prompt and JSON output schema (or name a workspace-defined operation with a persona resource); the parsed, schema-validated output is the step output; budget, approval mode and min_role apply exactly as for built-in operations.

branches.name: Conditional steps (if/else)
branches.acceptance: A step can declare `when` conditions evaluated against `steps.*` / `previous.*` (same operators as today); a false condition records the step as skipped (not failed) and later templates referencing it resolve to None; the dry run shows which branch would run.

iterate-aggregate.name: Iterate / aggregate over a target set
iterate-aggregate.acceptance: A target-selected set can be reduced into one output (`${target.rows}` / an aggregate step) so one step sees all rows, bounded by the target cap, with per-row errors recorded; a schedule trigger + target + aggregate step produces a digest payload in a dry run.

relative-dates.name: Relative dates and cron schedules
relative-dates.acceptance: `updated_before: "-30d"` (and `now`-relative `${…}` arithmetic) is accepted by entries/query.py `_when` and shown resolved in the preview; `schedule_type: cron` computes `next_run_at` with its timezone (croniter) and fires on the tick.

asset-resource-targets.name: Assets and resources as workflow subjects
asset-resource-targets.acceptance: asset_*/resource_* events hydrate `asset.*` / `resource.*` in the match context; an operation step with entity_type asset loads the image for vision ops and writes back `alt_text`; the target selector accepts entity asset|resource; derived assets record lineage (parent, operation, params).

workflow-approvals.name: Approval step inside a workflow

waits.name: Durable waits and delays
waits.acceptance: `{"kind": "wait", "until": "${entry.data.event_date} - 7d"}` persists the run, survives a restart, honours the workspace timezone and DST, can be cancelled, and resumes exactly once.

idempotency.name: Per-step idempotency keys
idempotency.acceptance: A webhook/integration step with `idempotency_key` (templated) that already succeeded for that key within the window is skipped and its recorded output reused; two concurrent duplicate events deliver once.

media-adapters.name: Image, file and audio processing adapters

fetch.name: HTTP fetch step
fetch.acceptance: A GET/HEAD step (SSRF-guarded, bounded body) returns status, headers and parsed body as step output; a link-check handler reports broken links for one entry.

social-adapters.name: Social publishing adapters

comments.name: Comment events

ops-triggers.name: Operational events as workflow triggers

joins.name: Parallel branches and joins

recipes.outcome: When an entry's status changes to the configured ready status it is posted to the client's intake endpoint; the endpoint's JSON response is stored on the entry as the receipt.

setup_variables.name: entry_type
setup_variables.description: Slug of the entry type that is handed to the client.

setup_variables.name: ready_status
setup_variables.description: The status that means “ready for the client” — one of Marvin's statuses: needs_review, approved, published.

setup_variables.name: handoff_webhook_id
setup_variables.description: Id of the outgoing webhook (type `workflow`) pointing at the client's intake endpoint. Its JSON response is stored as the receipt.

supporting_objects.name: Client intake
supporting_objects.purpose: The client's intake endpoint; its JSON response is the receipt.
supporting_objects.notes: `webhook_type: workflow` means it fires only from a workflow step. Headers may carry `{{SECRET_SLUG}}` references (UPPER_CASE: a workspace secret, resolved when the step runs). Leave `custom_payload` empty to send the step's body; set it to replace the body.

setup_variables.name: handoff_url
setup_variables.description: The endpoint the webhook posts to.

side_effects.description: POSTs entry id, title, url, status and the entry's data fields to the configured outgoing webhook (one attempt, 15 s timeout, no retry).
Merges handoff.status_code / receipt / run into the entry's metadata (emits entry_updated at depth+1; other workflows on entry_updated will see it).

recipes.failure_behaviour: The webhook step makes one attempt; a non-2xx or a timeout fails the run (recorded in the run history, `workflow_failed` alert if enabled) and the metadata step after it does not run. Re-publishing re-sends: there is no per-step idempotency key. A non-JSON response is stored as trimmed text.

dependencies.name: Per-step idempotency keys
dependencies.acceptance: A webhook/integration step with `idempotency_key` (templated) that already succeeded for that key within the window is skipped and its recorded output reused; two concurrent duplicate events deliver once.
dependencies.why: to never hand off the same version twice

notes: `ready_status` must be one of Marvin's statuses (needs_review, approved, published); `changed_to` fires once on the transition.
The whole `entry.data` object is sent — review what the type's fields contain before enabling.

brief.flow: Ready entry → configured handoff webhook → record receipt

dependencies.name: Collection-scoped steps
dependencies.acceptance: A step can read a collection's entries (`${collection.entries}`) and an operation can run over that set to produce one output (summary, roundup).
dependencies.why: a summary of the collection itself

dependencies.name: Create-entry action
dependencies.acceptance: An entry step `{"op": "create", "entry_type": …, "title": …, "data": {…}, "status": "draft"}` creates a schema-validated entry, returns `entry_id`/`slug` as step output, emits entry_created at depth+1, previews in a dry run, and never duplicates on a retried run (idempotency key = run + step).

notes: A narrower reading of the brief: the entry's summary is refreshed, not the collection's (a collection has no summary field and no step can read a collection's entries). A themed roundup needs collection-scope + create-entry.
The event carries `collection_name` (not the slug), so the condition compares the name.

brief.flow: Refresh collection summary or propose a themed social roundup

recipes.outcome: A manual run selects every published entry that has an image attached and moves each back to draft.

recipes.title: Every hour, rebuild the site
recipes.outcome: On an interval, a site rebuild is requested; Marvin coalesces requests and sends one webhook_triggered to the deploy target.

setup_variables.name: interval_seconds
setup_variables.description: Seconds between rebuild requests (3600 = hourly). Cron schedules are accepted but do not fire yet.

features: a deploy target (an event-driven outgoing webhook or integration subscription on webhook_triggered) for the rebuild to reach anything

supporting_objects.name: Workflow: Every hour, rebuild the site
supporting_objects.purpose: Created and kept in sync automatically from the schedule trigger (slug wf-<automation id>, task_type run_automation). Nothing to provision.

side_effects.description: Indirect: the coalesced rebuild calls the deploy hook (host build minutes).

recipes.failure_behaviour: A failing run does not fail the backing scheduled task; it is reported as automation_failed (the `workflow_failed` alert).
notes: Interval and once schedules fire; `cron` is accepted but never computes a next run (croniter is not a dependency).
The schedule's own run has no event: `${event.*}` is empty and conditions are skipped (a `target` still applies).

recipes.title: A webhook call finds an entry by slug and archives it
recipes.outcome: An external system POSTs `{"slug": …}` to an incoming webhook URL; the named entry is archived, or sent to review with the error when it can't be.

setup_variables.name: incoming_webhook
setup_variables.description: Slug of the incoming webhook that carries `{"slug": …}` in its body, or `any`.

supporting_objects.name: Archive requests
supporting_objects.purpose: The tokened URL the external system calls.
supporting_objects.notes: The request body becomes `${event.payload.*}`; headers and query string are not carried. Signature verification is optional but recommended.

side_effects.description: Archives the entry (emits entry_updated + entry_archived; entry_unpublished too when it was published).
Moves the entry to Needs review and appends a reason to metadata.review_reasons (emits entry_updated at depth+1).

recipes.failure_behaviour: An unknown slug fails the archive step and the on_failure step alike (no entry to flag): the run is recorded failed. Duplicate deliveries archive an already-archived entry again (no-op status-wise, but entry_updated fires).
notes: `webhook: any` matches every incoming webhook of the workspace; name one slug to scope it.

recipes.title: Trash every unattached image
recipes.outcome: A manual run moves every image that no entry uses into the Trash, where it can be restored until the Trash is emptied.

side_effects.description: Trashes each matched asset (emits asset_trashed per row); the file stays in storage until the Trash is emptied.

recipes.failure_behaviour: Capped at 250 assets per run (the preview shows the true count); assets already in the Trash are never selected, so a second run does nothing.
notes: A bare `trash` step acts on the current item: its entity_type follows the target.
Dry-run it first: POST /api/automations/{id}/run?dry_run=true lists the assets it would touch.

recipes.title: Restore all resources in the Trash
recipes.outcome: A manual run takes every trashed resource back out of the Trash.

side_effects.description: Restores each trashed resource (emits resource_restored per row; a site rebuild is queued when a visible item comes back and a deploy target exists).

recipes.failure_behaviour: Capped at 250 resources per run; only rows still in the Trash are selected, so it is safe to run again.
notes: `trashed: true` is the only way a target reaches the Trash; every other query leaves trashed rows out.

recipes.title: Post new uploads to a chat channel
recipes.outcome: Every upload is announced in a chat channel with its type, name, MIME type and public URL.

setup_variables.name: upload_webhook_id
setup_variables.description: Id of the outgoing webhook (Settings → Webhooks, type `workflow`) whose URL is your chat channel's incoming webhook (Slack, Discord, Mattermost…). Its own `custom_payload`, when set, replaces the body above.

supporting_objects.name: Uploads channel
supporting_objects.purpose: The chat channel's incoming-webhook URL.
supporting_objects.notes: The channel URL lives in the webhook row, not in the workflow: it works like a password. `webhook_type: workflow` means it fires only from a workflow step.

setup_variables.name: upload_channel_url
setup_variables.description: The chat channel's incoming-webhook URL.

side_effects.description: POSTs `{"text": …}` to the configured outgoing webhook once per upload (one attempt, 15 s timeout, no retry).

notes: `${asset.url}` is the public URL when the storage provider serves one, otherwise empty.
